<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Given a small category $\mathcal{T}$,
  the large category of small \textcolor{violet}{$\mathcal{T}$-categories} is given by the diagram category
  \[ \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}} \coloneqq \operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Cat}^{}) \]
  and the category of \textcolor{violet}{$\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{}} the presheaf category
  \[
    \mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}} \coloneqq \operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{An}^{}) \,.
  \]
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
We also consider the \textcolor{violet}{large $\mathcal{T}$-categories}, i.e. $\mathrm{CAT}^{\mathcal{T}}\coloneqq\mathrm{Fun}(\mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{CAT}^{})$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:coeff}
  Given a category $\mathcal C$, we define the \textcolor{violet}{$\mathcal{T}$-category of coefficient systems} via diagram categories indexed by slices:
  \[
    \underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}(\mathcal C) \colon \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}} \xrightarrow{\;\;\;\;\; (\mathcal{T}_{/\bullet})^{\mathrm{op}} \;\;\;\;\;} \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{op}} \xrightarrow{\;\;\;\;\; \operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(-,\mathcal C \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \;\;\;\;\;} \mathrm{Cat}^{}.
  \]
  Informally, the $V$-objects of $\underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}(\mathcal C)$ are given by the ``$V$-equivariant coefficient systems'' $(\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}} \rightarrow \mathcal C$, with restrictions functors given by precomposition along the ``induction functor'' $f_!\colon (\mathcal{T}_{/U})^{\mathrm{op}} \rightarrow (\mathcal{T}_{/V})^{\mathrm{op}}$ induced by a map $f\colon U \rightarrow V$ in $\mathcal{T}$.

  Correspondingly, we write $\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{} \coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}(\mathrm{Cat}^{})$ and $\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{} \coloneqq \underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}(\mathrm{An}^{})$ for the $\mathcal{T}$-categories of (small) $\mathcal{T}$-categories and $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{}.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
We refer to the objects in the image of the Yoneda embedding $\mathcal{T} \to \mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}$ as \textcolor{violet}{orbits}.
  The category of \textcolor{violet}{orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{}} is defined via finite-coproduct-cocompletion
  \[
    \mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \coloneqq {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\{\coprod_{i = 0}^n V_i \;\; \middle| \;\; V_i \in \mathcal{T}, n \in \mathbb{N}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright\}} \subset \mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}.
  \]
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
We say that a morphism of $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ is \textcolor{violet}{$\mathcal{N}$-admissible} if, for each fibre square
  \[
      \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
        f^{-1}(V) \& Y \\
        V \& X
        \arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        \arrow["{f_V}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
        \arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
        \arrow["f"', from=1-2, to=2-2]
        \arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2, "\iota"]
      \end{tikzcd}
  \]
  such that $V$ is an orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-anima, $f_V$ lies in $\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}}$.

  A wide subcategory $\mathcal{N} \subset \mathcal{T}$ is said to be an \textcolor{violet}{orbital subcategory} if $\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}} \subset \mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{}$ consists precisely of the $\mathcal{N}$-admissible maps;
  $\mathcal{N}$ is additionally \textcolor{violet}{atomic} if all maps in $\mathcal{N}$ which admit a section in $\mathcal{T}$ are equivalences.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rmk:N-adm-F}
  Choosing $\iota$ to be the identity, it follows that all $\mathcal{N}$-admissible maps between orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} lie in $\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ regardless of orbitality;
  in particular, our definition recovers {\cite[\href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08240v2\#theorem.4.2.2}{Def.~4.2.2}]{cll23}} by {\cite[\href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08240v2\#theorem.4.3.2}{Lem.~4.3.2}]{cll23}}.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
\label{example:orb_G}
    For $G$ a compact Lie group, we can choose $\mathcal{T}$ to be the orbit category $\mathrm{Orb}_{G}$ of $G$ -- the category of transitive $G$-{animæ}{} -- and $\mathcal{N}\coloneqq \mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{fin}}$ to be the class of maps with finite fibres. 
    It follows by the double coset formula that this is an orbital subcategory;
    all endomorphisms are isomorphisms in $\mathrm{Orb}_{G}$, so it is moreover atomic.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{ex:transf}
    In the case that $\mathcal{T}$ is already atomic orbital, \cite[Rmk.~I.1.99]{nat-thesis} shows that atomic orbital subcategories $\mathcal{N} \subset \mathcal{T}$ specialise to Blumbereg--Hill-Rubin's \textit{transfer systems} \cite{Blumberg-op,Rubin};
    in particular, under \cite[Thm.~I.4.15,Prop.~I.1.97]{nat-thesis}, they enumerate a poset of \textit{sub-terminal  $\mathcal{T}$-operads admitting a map from $
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{\infty}}{\mathbb{E}_{\infty,}}
$}.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
Similarly to \Cref{ex:transf}, atomic orbital subcategories of the \textit{Global indexing category} for compact Lie groups have been studied under the name \textit{global transfer systems} \cite[Def.~4.3]{Barrero_2023,Barrero_ab}.
<!-- end example-4 -->

<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
A (small) \textcolor{violet}{$\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category} is a finite product-preserving functor ${\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{}.$
    We write
    \[
        \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \subseteq \operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft({\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}}, \mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}
    \]
    for the full subcategory of $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-categories.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rmk:monoidality-of-fp}
      For all $V \in \mathcal{T}$, there exists an essentially unique product-preserving functor $\iota_V\colon \operatorname{Span}(\mathbb{F}) \hookrightarrow {\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}$ sending $* \mapsto V$;
      we acquire an evaluation functor 
      \[
      (-)^V = \iota_V^*\colon \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{}_\otimes \, ,
      \] endowing $\underline{\mathcal C}^V$ with a natural symmetric monoidal structure with unit $\mathbf{1}_V \in \underline{\mathcal C}$ and binary multiplication $\nabla_{\otimes}$, for $\nabla\colon 2 \cdot V \rightarrow V$ the fold map.

      This structure is canonical;
      indeed, ${\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}$ is semiadditive by \Cite[Lem.~C.3]{bh21}, so the universal property of commutative monoids yields an equivalence
      \begin{equation}\label{eq:cmon-lift}
        \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \simeq \operatorname{Fun}^\times{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft({\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}}, \mathrm{CMon}(\mathrm{Cat}^{}) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)},
      \end{equation}
      so that $w_{\otimes}$ and $w^*$ are naturally symmetric monoidal.
      The Eckmann-Hilton argument $\mathrm{CMon}(-) \simeq \mathrm{CMon}\mathrm{CMon}(-)$ (which is itself \eqref{eq:cmon-lift} for $\mathcal{T} \simeq *$) identifies the value of \eqref{eq:cmon-lift} on $V$ with the above symmetric monoidal structure on $\underline{\mathcal C}^V$.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
A $\mathcal{T}$-category \textcolor{violet}{admits $\mathcal{N}$-indexed products} if its associated functor  ${\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{op}} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{}$
    is \textcolor{violet}{right $\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}}$-adjointable};
    that is, for all cospans $u\colon U \rightarrow V \leftarrow W 
        \nobreak
        \mskip6mu plus1mu
        \mathpunct{} 
        \nonscript
        \mkern-\thinmuskip
        {:} 
        \mskip2mu
        \relax
 w$ with $w$ $\mathcal{N}$-admissible, $w^*$ admits a right adjoint $w_*$ whose Beck-Chevalley transformation
    \[
        u^* w_* \implies \overline{w}_* \overline{u}^*
    \]
    is an equivalence.
    We say that a functor $F \colon \underline{\mathcal C} \to \underline{\mathcal D}$ \textcolor{violet}{preserves $\mathcal{N}$-indexed products} if the Beck-Chevalley transformation
    \[ F w_\ast^{\underline{\mathcal C}} \Longrightarrow w_\ast^{\underline{\mathcal D}} F \colon \underline{\mathcal C}^V \longrightarrow \underline{\mathcal D}^W \] is an equivalence.
    We write $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathcal{N}-\times}(\underline{\mathcal C},\underline{\mathcal D}) \subset \operatorname{Fun}(\underline{\mathcal C},\underline{\mathcal D})$ for the subcategory of $\mathcal{N}$-indexed product preserving functors and we write $\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\times} \subset \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}$ for the non-full subcategory of $\mathcal{T}$-categories with $\mathcal{N}$-indexed products and $\mathcal{T}$-functors preserving them.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- construction-1: body_md -->
Stefanich \cite[Thm.~1.1.1]{stefanich} provides the universal property for the $(\infty,2)$-category of spans which, after restricting to core categories, yields a map
    \[
        \mathrm{Map}_{\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}}-\mathrm{Radj}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{}, \mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Map}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft({\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}}, \mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)};
    \]
    since ${\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{op}} \hookrightarrow {\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}$ creates products, this restricts to a map of {animæ}{}                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                               
    \[
        {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(- \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^\times\colon {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\times} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^\simeq \longrightarrow {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^\simeq.
    \]
<!-- end construction-1 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\cite[Thm.~II.2.1]{nat-thesis} confirms that the above cartesian structure generalises \cite[Ex.~2.4.1]{NS}.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- construction-2: body_md -->
We now explain how to assemble $\mathrm{Cat}^{V}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes}$ into a $\mathcal{T}$-category. Note that there exists an equivalence $\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}_{/V}}_{} \simeq \mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}$;
    thus postcomposition yields a functor
    \[
        \widetilde{\mathbb{F}}\colon  \mathcal{T}^{\triangleright} 
        \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{},
    \]
    with cocone value $\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{}$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{F}}(V) \simeq \mathbb{F}^V$.
    Writing $\mathbb{F}^{V}_{\mathcal{N}} \subset \mathbb{F}^{V}_{}$ for the preimages of $\mathcal{N}$-admissible maps, these are the $\mathcal{N}_V$-admissible maps for the atomic orbital subcategory $\mathcal{N}_V \rightarrow \mathcal{T}_{/V}$ of preimages of $\mathcal{N}$-maps (see \cite[Prop.~I.1.97,Prop.~I.1.113]{nat-thesis}). 
    In particular, applying this functoriality yields a $\mathcal{T}$-category
    \[
        \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes}\colon \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{op}} \xrightarrow{\;\;\;\; \widetilde{\mathbb{F}}_{\mathcal{N}} \subset \widetilde{\mathbb{F}} \;\;\;\;} \mathrm{SpanPair}^{\mathrm{op}} \xrightarrow{\;\;\;\; \mathrm{Span}_{(-)}(-) \;\;\;\;}  \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathrm{op}} \xrightarrow{\;\;\;\; \operatorname{Fun}^\times {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(-,\mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}  \;\;\;\;} \mathrm{CAT}^{},
    \]
    such that $\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \simeq \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes}$ and $\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{V}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \simeq \mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}_{/V}}_{\mathcal{N}_V-\otimes}$.
<!-- end construction-2 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
Let $\underline{\mathcal C} , \underline{\mathcal D} \colon {\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{}$ be $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-categories. A \textcolor{violet}{lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor} is a functor of their cocartesian unstraightenings
    \[ \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=small]
        \int \underline{\mathcal C} \ar[rr] \ar[dr] & & \int \underline{\mathcal D} \ar[dl] \\
        & {\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}
    \end{tikzcd} \] 
    which  preserves cocartesian lifts of backwards maps. 

    Note that $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-categories have a \textcolor{violet}{fibrewise opposite} involution 
    \[
        {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(- \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{op}} \colon \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \longrightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes}
    \]
    gotten by applying $(-)^{\mathrm{op}}$ fibrewise.
    We define an \textcolor{violet}{oplax $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor} $\underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow  \underline{\mathcal D}$ to simply be a lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed functor $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\underline{\mathcal C}{^{\mathrm{op}}} \to \underline{\mathcal D}{^{\mathrm{op}}}$.
    
    In the case where $\underline{\mathcal C}$ is the terminal $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category, we call a lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal D}$ a \textcolor{violet}{normed algebra in $\underline{\mathcal D}$}; 
    that is, normed algebras are defined to be sections of the cocartesian unstraightening which are cocartesian on backwards morphisms.
<!-- end definition-6 -->

<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
The proof of \Cref{prop:cart} uses atomicity in an integral way, hence our ongoing assumption that we are normed along an atomic orbital subcategory.
<!-- end remark-6 -->

<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:monoidal-structure-Bousfield-loc}
    Let $\underline{\mathcal C}$ be an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category, and $L\colon \underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal{B}}$ a Bousfield localisation such that the $\mathcal{T}$-class of $L$-equivalences is closed under $\mathcal{N}$-norms.
    Then, $\underline{\mathcal{B}}$ and $L$ jointly uniquely lift to an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category and $\mathcal{N}$-normed functor.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->

\ar[d,"{(-)^{\triangleright}}"] \\
{\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}}_{/\underline{\mathcal C}} \ar[r] & \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{} \end{tikzcd} \]

  \relax

Indeed, letting $\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{\ast} \subset \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}$ denote the (non-full) $\mathcal{T}$-subcategory spanned by $V$-categories with a terminal object and $V$-functors preserving them, 
this $\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{\ast}$ is closed under indexed products, so that the above inclusion enhances to a cartesian $\mathcal{N}$-normed functor. 
It admits $(-)^{\triangleright} \colon \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{} \longrightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{\ast}$ as a left adjoint, which is given an oplax $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure by the doctrinal adjunction \cite[Prop.~I.3.6]{nat-thesis}\footnote{This proposition statement has a typo; in its notation, and in the proof, $F$ is assumed to be \textit{lax}, not oplax.}. The oplax $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor in question now arises as the composite of this left adjoint and the inclusion.

\label{def:norm-cocart-fib}
    An $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\varphi\colon \underline{\mathcal D} \to \underline{\mathcal C}$ is called an \textcolor{violet}{$\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibration} if $\underline{\mathcal D}^V \to \underline{\mathcal C}^V$ is a cocartesian fibration for all orbits $V$ and $\varphi$-cocartesian arrows are closed under restrictions and $\mathcal{N}$-norms.

<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
For any $V$, the subcategory inclusions in $\mathrm{CAT}^{V}$ are the right part of a factorisation system (together with the essentially surjective functors) and these factorisation systems are compatible with restrictions and norms. It follows from \cite[Prop.~6.7]{lnp25} that the functor $t \colon \underline{\mathrm{FSub}\mathrm{CAT}^{}}^V \to \mathrm{Cat}^{V}$ is a cocartesian fibration. It also follows from the description of the cocartesian arrows in \textit{loc. cit.} that the cocartesian arrows are closed under restriction and under norms.
<!-- end proof-2 -->

<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:dist-compose} \label{lem:postcomposing_distributive_with_colimit_pres}
  Given a subcategory $\underline{\mathcal{K}} \subset U^\ast \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}$ and a composable sequence of $\mathcal{N}$-admissible maps $U \xrightarrow{u} W \xrightarrow{w} V$ and a $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-cocomplete $U$-category $\underline{\mathcal C}$, a $u_\ast \underline{\mathcal{K}}$-cocomplete $W$-category $\underline{\mathcal D}$ and $(wu)_\ast \underline{\mathcal{K}}$-cocomplete $V$-category $\underline{\mathcal E}$. 
  Let $F \colon w_\ast \underline{\mathcal D} \to \underline{\mathcal E}$ and $G \colon u_\ast \underline{\mathcal C} \to \underline{\mathcal D}$ be $u_*\underline{\mathcal{K}}$- and $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive multifunctors. Then $F \circ w_\ast G \colon (wu)_\ast \underline{\mathcal C} \to \underline{\mathcal E}$ is $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->

<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:distributive-category}
    For $\underline{\mathcal{K}} \subset \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}$, an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category $\underline{\mathcal C}$ is called \textcolor{violet}{$\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive} if for all $\mathcal{N}$-admissible maps of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} $w \colon W \to V$, the $w$-norm $w$-multifunctor 
    \[ w_{\otimes} \colon w_{\ast} W^\ast \underline{\mathcal C} \longrightarrow V^\ast \underline{\mathcal C} \] is $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive. 
    In the case where $\underline{\mathcal{K}}=\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}$, we say $\underline{\mathcal C}$ is \textcolor{violet}{distributive}.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:transf_examples}
    Let $\varphi\colon \underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal D}$ be a $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-cocontinuous $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor between $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-categories.
    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\arabic*)]
        \item If $\varphi$ is conservative and $\underline{\mathcal D}$ is $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive, then $\underline{\mathcal C}$ is $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive.
        \item If $\varphi$ is a Bousfield localisation and $\underline{\mathcal C}$ is $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive, then $\underline{\mathcal D}$ is $\underline{\mathcal{K}}$-distributive.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->

    Distributivity of $\underline{\mathcal D}$ implies $\beta_{\overline{w}^{\underline{\mathcal D}}_{\otimes}, \varphi \circ m}$ is an equivalence, so conservativity implies that $\beta_{\overline{w}^{\underline{\mathcal C}}_{\otimes}, m}$ is an equivalence, yielding distributivity of $\underline{\mathcal C}$ under \Cref{rmk:assembly-map}.

<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:distributivity_of_cartesian_symmon}
    Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a category which admits finite products. 
    Then $\underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}(\mathcal{D})\in \mathrm{CAT}^{\mathcal{T}}$  admits finite $\mathcal{N}$-indexed products. Moreover, if  $\mathcal{D}$ is additionally a cocomplete category and the product bifunctor commutes with colimits separately in each variable, then $\underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}(\mathcal{D})\in \mathrm{CAT}^{\mathcal{T}}$ is also cocomplete and its cartesian $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure is distributive.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->

<!-- construction-8: body_md -->
\label{cons:subcategoriesOfHornPowers}
    We write the inclusion $\Lambda^2_0\subseteq (\Delta^1)^{\times2}$ as 
    \begin{center}
      \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=scriptsize]
            00 \rar\dar & 10 \ar[drr, phantom, "\hookrightarrow"]&& 00 \rar \dar& 10\dar \\
            01 & && 01 \rar & 11
        \end{tikzcd}
    \end{center}
    In this way, for any $n\geq 1$, we may denote the objects in the full subcategory $\prod^n_{i=1}\Lambda^2_0\subseteq \prod^n_{i=1}(\Delta^1)^{\times2}$ as those tuples $(a_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ where $a_i\in\{00,10,01\}$. We want to decompose $\prod^n_{i=1}\Lambda^2_0$ in terms of subcategories that we will now specify:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Let $M_n\subseteq \prod^n_{i=1}\Lambda^2_0$ be the full subcategory $\prod^n_{i=1}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\Delta^1\times\{0\}\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)$. Concretely in terms of the tuples description above, this is the full subcategory consisting of those tuples such that $a_i\in\{00,10\}$.
        \item Let $B_n\subseteq \prod^n_{i=1}\Lambda^2_0$ be the full subcategory $\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\prod^n_{i=1}\Lambda^2_0\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)\backslash \{(10,\ldots,10)\}$, i.e. of those tuples where some of the $a_i$'s must either be $00$ or $01$.
        \item Let $F_n\subseteq B_n$ be the full subcategory of those tuples where $a_i\in\{01,10\}$, that is, where none of the $a_i$'s are $00$ and at least one of them is $01$. 
        \item Let $J_n\coloneqq M_n\cap B_n$, that is, where $a_i \in \{00,10\}$ but not all are $10$.
    \end{itemize}
    Similarly, since for any map $w\colon W\rightarrow V$ in $\mathcal{N}$,  $w_*\underline{\Lambda}^2_0$ is fibrewise just products of multiple copies of $\Lambda^2_0$, we may similarly define in a fibrewise fashion the $V$--full subcategories $\underline{J}_w, \underline{F}_w, \underline{B}_w,\underline{M}_w\subseteq w_*\underline{\Lambda}^2_0$. Here, $\underline{J}_w,\underline{B}_w, \underline{M}_w$ are clearly $V$--subcategories, and $\underline{F}_w$ is too  by the exact same argument as in \cite[Cons. 3.2.3]{kaifNoncommMotives}. 
    Moreover, the  $\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}$-square \begin{equation}\label{obs:pushoutDecompositionOfHornPowers}
      \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=scriptsize]
            \underline{J}_w \rar[hook]\dar[hook]\ar[dr,phantom,very near end, "\ulcorner"] & \underline{M}_w\dar[hook]\\
            \underline{B}_w\rar[hook] & w_*\underline{\Lambda}^2_0
        \end{tikzcd}
    \end{equation}
   is a pushout; 
   indeed pushouts may be checked fibrewise, which is \cite[Obs. 3.2.4]{kaifNoncommMotives}.
<!-- end construction-8 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:F_fB_fAdjunction}
    The inclusion of $\mathcal{T}$--categories $\underline{F}_w\subseteq \underline{B}_w$ is cofinal, i.e. restriction along it induces a natural equivalence $\operatorname*{colim}_{\underline{B}_w}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(- \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}\xrightarrow{\;\;\; \sim \;\;\;} \operatorname*{colim}_{\underline{F}_w}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(- \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Parametrised cofinality is checked fibrewise \cite[Thm. 6.7]{Sha23}, and the fibrewise statement is given by \cite[Lem. 3.2.5]{kaifNoncommMotives}.

\label{lem:fast-left-fibration}
    Let $f \colon T \to S$ be a map of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{}. and $\pi\colon \underline{\mathcal D} \to \underline{\mathcal C}$ a left fibration of $T$-categories with straightening $T$-functor $F\colon \underline{\mathcal C} \to T^*\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}$.  
    Then $f_* \pi\colon f_\ast \underline{\mathcal D} \to f_\ast \underline{\mathcal C}$ straightens to the composite $F\colon f_\ast \underline{\mathcal C} \to f_\ast T^*\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{} \simeq f_* f^* S^* \xrightarrow{\text{limit}} S^*\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}$.

 / } \to f_\ast T^*\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}$. This straightens to the functor taking maps out of the terminal object in $f_\ast T^* \underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}$ which indeed represents taking the limit.

    Now an arbitrary left fibration is pulled back from the universal left fibration along its straightening by \cite[Cor.~3.3.2.7]{lur09}, and the unstraightening of left $\mathcal{T}$-fibrations are left fibrations, so the mapping-in property of coefficient systems yields the lefthand pullback square of $\mathcal{T}$-categories
\[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, row sep=small]
	\underline{\mathcal D} \& \underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{} \&\& {\int \underline{\mathcal D}} \& \mathrm{An}^{}_\ast \\
	\underline{\mathcal C} \& \underline{\mathrm{An}}^{} \&\& {\int \underline{\mathcal C}} \& \mathrm{An}^{}
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-4, to=2-5]
	\arrow[from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=2-4, to=2-5]
	\arrow[between={0.2}{0.8}, squiggly, tail reversed, no head, from=0, to=1]
\end{tikzcd}\]
  This pullback is preserved by $f_\ast$, proving the claim.

<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By \Cref{cor:triangle_of_indexed_yoneda}, we clearly have the diagram when we replace $(w_*\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\underline{\mathcal A}})_!$ and $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\underline{\mathcal A}!}$ with their right adjoints $(w_*\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\underline{\mathcal A}})^*$ and $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\underline{\mathcal A}}^*$ respectively. 
    The map on the left is an equivalence by \Cref{prop:presheaf-dist}, and so is the one on the right by the universal property of the Yoneda embedding by \cite[Thm. 7.1.1]{MartiniWolf2024}. 
    We conclude that all maps are equivalences, and passing to inverses yields the conclusion.
<!-- end proof-19 -->

    where the vertical arrows are induced by the forgetful functor and the horizontal by postcomposition. 
    The vertical arrows are monomorphisms by \Cref{Catcocone-subcat} and the lower arrow is a monomorphism as $\underline{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{proj}} \subset \underline{\mathcal C}$ is a $\mathcal{T}$-subcategory inclusion.

\label{lem:filt-lim-commute}
    Let $\kappa$ be $\mathcal{T}$-restrictible. Then $\mathrm{infl}^{\mathcal{T}}_{}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathrm{filt}(\kappa)\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)$-colimits commute with $\kappa$-small limits in $\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}$;
    hence, for any $\mathcal{T}$-category $\underline{\mathcal C}$, $\underline{\mathcal C}^{\kappa} \subset \underline{\mathcal C}$ is closed under $\kappa$-small colimits.

<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
By the description of \cite[Prop.~I.2.65,Cor.~I.2.67]{nat-thesis} (and filteredness of total orders), we must show that  
     every presentable $\mathcal{T}$-category is $\kappa$-accessible for some $\mathcal{N}$-normable $\kappa$ and every left adjoint of presentable $\mathcal{T}$-categories preserves $\kappa$-compact objects for some $\mathcal{N}$-normable $\kappa$;
    equivalently, every right adjoint of presentable $\mathcal{T}$-categories is $\kappa$-accessible.
    That this holds for Martini-Wolf's ``sound doctrines'' is \cite[Cor.~2.4.1.8,Prop.~2.4.3.3]{mwpresentable};
    that it is true for uncountable $\mathcal{N}$-normable cardinals is then  \Cref{rmk:cofin}.
<!-- end proof-39 -->

Next, observe that $\mathrm{idem}\in\mathrm{Cat}^{}$  is filtered (hence sifted), so $\mathrm{infl}^{\mathcal{T}}_{}\mathrm{idem}$-distributivity is reduced to a fibrewise $\mathrm{idem}$-colimit preservation  by \Cref{prop:dist-lemmas}. But then all functors  preserve $\mathrm{idem}$-colimits since these are absolute colimits.

<!-- example-7: body_md -->
If $\mathcal{T}$ is atomic orbital, we claim that all regular cardinals $\kappa$ are $\mathcal{T}$-restrictable;
    indeed the characterisation of \Cref{prop:kappa-restricts} reduces this to the observation that
    $U \times_V X \in \mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{}$ is finite for all orbits $U,V,X$, which is clear.
    It is, however, not clear that $\kappa$ is always $\mathcal{T}$-normable, and we suspect that this is not the case.
<!-- end example-7 -->

    \begin{enumerate}[label={(\alph*)}]
      \item \label[condition]{cond:unit-idem} the $\mathbb{E}_0$-algebra $\eta\colon \mathbf{1}\rightarrow Y$ is $\mathcal{N}$-idempotent;
      \item \label[condition]{cond:modules-idem} the $\mathbb{E}_0$-algebra $\eta\colon \mathbf{1}\rightarrow Y$ is idempotent and, for all $\mathcal{N}$-admissible maps $w\colon W \rightarrow V$, $V^*Y$ admits the structure of a module over the unique idempotent commutative algebra structure on $\mathbf{1}\rightarrow w_{\otimes}W^*Y$;
        \item the $\mathbb{E}_0$-algebra $\eta\colon \mathbf{1}\rightarrow Y$ is idempotent and the smashing localisation $L = -\otimes Y\colon \underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow \underline{\operatorname{Mod}}_{Y}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\underline{\mathcal C} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}$ is $\mathcal{N}$-normed; or
        \item the $\mathbb{E}_0$-algebra $\eta\colon \mathbf{1}\rightarrow Y$ is idempotent and refines to the unit of an $\mathcal{N}$-normed algebra structure on $Y$.
    \end{enumerate}

<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
The left-hand side is equivalent to the fibres of the pullback functor on categories of algebras over $Y$, applied to the map of operads $
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{\infty}}{\mathbb{E}_{\infty,}}
 \simeq 
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{\infty}}{\mathbb{E}_{\infty,}}
 \times_{
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{1}}{\mathbb{E}_{1,}}
} 
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{1}}{\mathbb{E}_{1,}}
 \rightarrow 
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{\infty}}{\mathbb{E}_{\infty,}}
 \times_{
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{1}}{\mathbb{E}_{1,}}
} \mathrm{LMod}$;
    but by \cite[Cor.~I.4.38]{nat-thesis} these are the $\mathcal{T}$-objects in the fibre of the associated map of inflated parametrised operads, whose algebra categories are simply defined fibrewise by operad algebras, and hence match the right-hand side.
<!-- end proof-43 -->

We first prove that the above conditions are equivalent.
    That (a) $\iff$ (b) is obvious in light of the characterisation of modules over idempotent algebras {\cite[\href{https://people.math.harvard.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf\#theorem.4.8.2.10}{Prop.~4.8.2.10}]{lur17}}.
    For showing (a) $\implies$ (c), let $w\colon W \rightarrow V$ be an $\mathcal{N}$-admissible map of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} and $\varphi\colon X \rightarrow Z$ an $L^W$-equivalence.
    We want to show that $V^*Y\otimes w_{\otimes}\varphi$ is an equivalence. By the hypothesis on $Y$, we know 
    \[
        V^*Y\otimes w_{\otimes}\varphi\simeq V^*Y\otimes w_{\otimes}W^*Y\otimes w_{\otimes}\varphi\simeq V^*Y\otimes w_{\otimes}(W^*Y\otimes \varphi),
    \]
    whence follows the desired conclusion. 
    
    Next,  (c) $\implies$ (a) is clear since $\mathbf{1}\rightarrow W^*Y$ is an $L$-equivalence by $\mathcal{N}$-idempotence of $\eta$.
    Now, (c) $\implies$ (d) because $Y$ is the image of the normed algebra $\mathbf{1}$ under the $\mathcal{N}$-normed localisation $L$ (see \cite[\S~I.3.4-6]{nat-thesis}).
    
    
    To finish identifying conditions, suppose (d).
    \cite[Cor.~III.1.8]{nat-thesis} shows that postcomposition along the $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\mathrm{CAlg}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\underline{\mathcal C} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \rightarrow  \underline{\mathcal C}$ under the pointwise structure provides an equivalence

{\mathrm{NAlg}}_{\mathcal{N}} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( \underline{\mathcal C} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{}}
,
    \]
    so a general normed algebra in $\underline{\mathcal C}$ admits refinements of its normed multiplication map $w_{\otimes}  W^* X \rightarrow V^* X$
    to a commutative algebra map.
    In particular, $V^*X$ is given a module structure over $w_{\otimes} W^* X$;
    this specialises to (b).
   
    Now, the fact that $U$ is fully faithful is follows from the mapping anima formula in \Cref{lem:NAlg-idem}; indeed, the morphism of mapping {animæ}{} induced by $U$ is always an endomorphism of $*$ or $\varnothing$, and
    these are all equivalences. 
    
    To describe the essential image, first observe that $UY$ certainly satisfies condition (a) since the composition $V^*Y\simeq V^*Y\otimes \mathbf{1} \xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}\otimes \eta} V^*Y\otimes w_{\otimes}W^*Y\xrightarrow{\mu} V^*Y$ is the identity map, and so the first map is an equivalence if and only if the second is. On the other hand, if an $
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{0}}{\mathbb{E}_{0,}}
$-algebra $\mathbf{1}\rightarrow Y$ satisfies any of the conditions, then in particular, it refines to an $\mathcal{N}$-normed algebra by (d). And then by (a)  and the above argument, it is idempotent. 
    
    Finally, \eqref{eq:relation-mod} and \eqref{eq:tensor-mod} follow directly from the  non-parametrised statements, which are shown in the proof of \cite[Prop. 4.8.2.9]{lur17} and in \cite[\href{https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/CSY2.pdf\#thm.5.1.8}{Prop.~5.1.8}]{csy20}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
\label{cor:contractibility-monoidal-structures}
    If $\eta\colon \underline{\mathrm{An}}^{} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal C}$ is an idempotent $
    \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
    {\mathbb{E}_{0}}{\mathbb{E}_{0,}}
$-algebra in $\underline{\Pr}^{L}$, then the following conditions are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}[label={(\alph*)}]
      \item the map $\eta$ witnesses $\underline{\mathcal C}$ as an $\mathcal{N}$-mode,
      \item the map $\eta$ refines to the unit of a distributive $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure, and
      \item the smashing localisation on $\underline{\Pr}^{L}$ classified by $\eta$ attains an $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure.
    \end{enumerate}
    In this case, the anima of distributive $\mathcal{N}$-normed structures on $\underline{\mathcal C}$ with unit  $\eta$ is contractible.
<!-- end corollary-12 -->

\label{lem:distributivity_pointed_cocompletionB}
    Let $w\colon W \rightarrow V$ be an $\mathcal{N}$-admissible map of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{}. There exists an equivalence $w_{\otimes}W^*\underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{}  \xrightarrow{\sim} V^*\underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{}$  participating in a commuting square
    \begin{equation}\label{comm-diagram-dist-based}
   \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&,column sep=large,row sep=scriptsize]
	{w_\otimes W^\ast \underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}} \& {V^\ast \underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}} \\
	{w_\otimes W^\ast \underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{}.} \& {V^\ast \underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{}}
	\arrow["\sim"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{w_\otimes W^\ast (-)+}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{V^\ast(-)_+}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\sim"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
    where the top horizontal equivalence is the $\mathcal{N}$-mode $w$-multiplication $V$-functor of $\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{}$.

<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:identify-inversions}
  Suppose $\underline{\mathcal D} \subset \underline{\mathcal E} \subset \underline{\mathcal C}$ are $\mathcal{T}$-sets of objects in a presentable $\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category $\underline{\mathcal C}$ whose  composite $\underline{\mathcal E} \hookrightarrow \underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal C}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[\underline{\mathcal D}^{-1} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright]}$
  takes values in $\otimes$-invertible objects.
  Then, the induced $\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\underline{\mathcal C}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[\underline{\mathcal E}^{-1} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright]} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal C}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[\underline{\mathcal D}^{-1} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright]}$ is an equivalence.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
It suffices to note that a $\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal{B}}$ inverts $\underline{\mathcal E}$ if and only if it inverts $\underline{\mathcal D}$;
  the backwards direction follows by factorisation through $\underline{\mathcal C}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[\underline{\mathcal D}^{-1} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright]}$.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
\label{rmk:point-set-smash}
    We will use a point-set model for the binary smash product of pointed $G$-{animæ}{}: \Cref{prop:formula_for_norms_in_pointed_anima} identifies the smash product within a cofibre sequence
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:smash-cofibre}
        X \vee Y \longrightarrow X \times Y \longrightarrow X \wedge Y
    \end{equation}
    in $\underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{G}$.
    Presenting $\underline{\mathrm{An}}_{\ast}^{G}$ as via the standard model structure on $\mathrm{Top}_{G,*}$, whenever the base-point inclusions $* \hookrightarrow X$ and $* \hookrightarrow Y$ are $G$-NDR pairs, so is $X \vee Y \hookrightarrow X \times Y$;
    hence it is a cofibration, and \eqref{eq:smash-cofibre} is the image of a cofibre sequence in $\mathrm{Top}_{G,*}$.
<!-- end remark-15 -->

<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{example:Lie-group}
    For $G$ a compact Lie group, \Cref{cor:norms-finite-cats} demonstrates that $\aleph_0$ is $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{fin}}$-normable. 
    Condition (a) of \Cref{prop:kappa-norms} shows that $\mathcal{N}$-normability of regular $\kappa$ is equivalent to having larger cardinality than the minimal $\mathcal{N}$-normable cardinal, so this implies that \textit{every} regular cardinal is $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{fin}}$-normable.
    In particular, \Cref{thm:ind} applies for $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{fin}}$-normed $G$-categories with no restriction on $\kappa$.
<!-- end remark-16 -->

<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:normed-straightening}
    Let $\underline{\mathcal C}$ be an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category. 
    There is an equivalence
    \[ 
        \mathrm{St}\colon {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathcal{N}-\otimes} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/\underline{\mathcal C}} \xrightarrow{\;\;\;\;\; \sim \;\;\;\;\;} \operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{lax}-\mathcal{N}-\otimes}(\underline{\mathcal C},\underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{\times}),
    \]
    natural in lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functors in $\underline{\mathcal C}$, such that 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item on underlying functors, $\mathrm{St}$ is given by the parametrised straightening, and
        \item for $\underline{\mathcal D} \to \underline{\mathcal C}$ an $\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibration, $w \colon W \to V$ an $\mathcal{N}$-admissible map of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{}, and $c \in \underline{\mathcal C}^W$, the lax structure map on the straightening $F \colon \underline{\mathcal C} \to \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{}$
        \[ 
            \ell_{w,c}\colon w_\ast F(c) \longrightarrow F(w_{\otimes}c) 
        \]
        has $W$-fixed points given by by restriction of the $w$-norm functor $w_{\otimes} \colon  \underline{\mathcal D}^W \to  \underline{\mathcal D}^V$ to the fibres over $c$ and $w_{\otimes} c$, respectively.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:fact_cocart}
    Suppose $\pi\colon \mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ is a functor and $\mathcal{B}^L, \mathcal{B}^R \subset\mathcal{B}$ is a factorisation system
    Then, $\pi$ is a cocartesian fibration if and only if the following conditions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\pi$ has cocartesian lifts over $\mathcal{B}^L$, and
        \item The pullback $\pi|_{\mathcal{B}^R}$ of $\pi$ along $\mathcal{B}^R \to \mathcal{B}$ is a cocartesian fibration.
        \item for all commutative square in $\mathcal{A}$
        \[ \begin{tikzcd}
            A \ar[r] \ar[d] & B \ar[d] \\
            C \ar[r] & D
        \end{tikzcd} \] where the horizontal arrows are cocartesian lifts over $\mathcal{B}^L$ and the vertical arrows lie over $\mathcal{B}^R$: if the right arrow is $\pi|{_{\mathcal{B}^R}}$-cocartesian, then so is the left one.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
For the \enquote{only if}-direction, the first two conditions follow from pullback stability of cocartesian fibrations, while the last condition follows from the dual of \cite[Prop.~2.4.17]{lur09}.
    
    For the \enquote{if}-direction, we use the dual of \cite[Prop.~4.4]{hhln23a} (which does not use the adequate condition stated in there), to see that there is a factorisation system on $\mathcal{A}$ where the right maps are the ones sent to $\mathcal{B}^R$ and the left maps are cocartesian lifts over $\mathcal{B}^L$. Conditions $1$ and $2$ precisely translate to the functor being the dual notion of an op-Gray fibration as defined in \cite[Def.~5.14]{hhln23a} (replacing cartesian by cocartesian).

    The proposition now precisely translates to \cite[Lem.~5.17]{hhln23a}. The result therein is stated for adequate factorisation system but the adequate condition is not used in the proof.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:two-cocarts}
    An $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\pi\colon \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal C}$ is an $\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibration if and only if the unstraightening $\int \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \int \underline{\mathcal C}$ is a (non-parametrised) cocartesian fibration.
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Note that $\int \underline{\mathcal C}\in \mathrm{Cat}^{}$ admits a factorisation system whose lefthand part is cocartesian arrows over ${\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}$ and righthand parts are the arrows in fibres  under \cite[Prop.~2.1.2.5]{lur17}.

    The restriction of $\pi$ to the preimage of $\int \underline{\mathcal C}^R$ is given by the disjoint union of $\underline{\mathcal D}^W \to \underline{\mathcal C}^W$ over all orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} $W$. 
    We have $\underline{\mathcal C}^W \simeq \prod_{U_i \in \mathrm{Orbits}(W)} \underline{\mathcal C}^{U_i}$, naturally in $\underline{\mathcal C}$, so that the functor $\underline{\mathcal D}^W \to \underline{\mathcal C}^W$ identifies with a product of various evaluations of the original functor. It therefore is a cocartesian fibration if the original $\mathcal{T}$-functor is a cocartesian fibration,
    whence  condition 2 of \Cref{lem:fact_cocart} with the underlying $\mathcal{T}$-functor being cocartesian.
    Condition 1 of \Cref{lem:fact_cocart} is identified with $\mathcal{N}$-normedness under {\cite[\href{https://kerodon.net/tag/01TK}{Tag 01TK}]{kerodon}}.
    Unwinding definitions identifies our closure hypothesis with condition 3 of  \Cref{lem:fact_cocart}, yielding the claim.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- notation-5: body_md -->
We write $U\underline{\mathcal C}$ for the underlying $\mathcal{T}$-category of an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category $\underline{\mathcal C}$.
<!-- end notation-5 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
We will temporarily denote cocartesian unstraightenings over $\mathcal{T}^{^{\mathrm{op}}}$ as $\int_{\mathcal{T}}$, and leave unstraightening over ${\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}$ undecorated.
    Consider the following commutative diagram:
\[
\adjustbox{max width=\textwidth}{
  \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
	\& P \& {\mathrm{Seg}_{\int \underline{\mathcal C}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}} \& {\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{lax}-\mathcal{N}-\otimes}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\underline{\mathcal C}, \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{\times} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}} \\
	\& {{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/\int \underline{\mathcal C}}} \& {\operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\int \underline{\mathcal C}, \mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}} \\
	{{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{\mathcal{T}} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/U\mathcal C}} \& {{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/\int_{\mathcal{T}} U\underline{\mathcal C}}} \& {\operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\int_{\mathcal{T}} U \underline{\mathcal C}, \mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}} \& {\operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(U\underline{\mathcal C}, \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}}
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3, "\sim"]
	\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[hook', from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\sim"', from=1-4, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=3-4]
	\arrow["\sim", from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-2, to=3-2]
	\arrow[from=2-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["\sim", from=3-1, to=3-2]
	\arrow["\sim", from=3-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["\sim", from=3-3, to=3-4]
\end{tikzcd}}
\] 

where the upper right equivalence is \cite[Thm.~II.2.1,Thm.~I.4.1,Prop.~I.3.4]{nat-thesis}, the lower left by \cite[Rmk.~7.4]{Sha23}, and the lower right by \cite[Thm.~7.8]{bdgns16}.
We must show that the pullback full subcategory $P \subset {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathrm{Cat}^{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/\int \underline{\mathcal C}}$ of cocartesian fibrations $\pi\colon \int \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \int \underline{\mathcal C}$ whose unstraightening is a Segal  $\int \underline{\mathcal C}$-object corresponds precisely with the $\mathcal{N}$-symmetric monodial cocartesian fibrations;
then, by examining the above diagram and noting that the bottom horizontal composite is (by definition) parametrised straightening, our equivalence will satisfy the first point.

In the language of algebraic patterns, we find ourself with a triangle
\[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&,column sep=large,row sep=tiny]
	{\int \underline{\mathcal D}} \&\& {\int \underline{\mathcal C}} \\
	\& {{\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}}
	\arrow["{\pi}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_{\underline{\mathcal D}}}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\pi_{\underline{\mathcal C}}}", from=1-3, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
such that $\pi_{\underline{\mathcal C}}$ is a cocartesian fibrous pattern.
By cancellation for fibrous patterns \cite[Prop.~4.1.16, Cor.~3.3.24]{bhs25}, we find that $\pi$ is a cocartesian fibrous pattern (i.e. Segal fibration \cite[Obs.~4.1.10,Lem.~4.1.15]{bhs25}) if and only if the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\alph*)}]
    \item $\pi$ is a cocartesian fibration, and
    \item $\pi_{\underline{\mathcal D}}$ is fibrous pattern.
\end{enumerate}  
    But by composing cocartesian fibrations, condition (b) may be replaced with $\pi_{\underline{\mathcal D}} $ being a Segal fibration.
    This identifies $P$ with the $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functors $\underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal C}$ becoming cocartesian fibrations under $\int$;
    these are precisely the $\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibrations by \Cref{lem:two-cocarts}.

    We are left with the second point.
    Recall that the ``Segal object'' embedding, considered with codomain all functors, factors as follows:\[
        \operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{lax-\mathcal{N}-\otimes}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\underline{\mathcal C},\underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathcal{B} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}^\times \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \rightarrow \operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\int \underline{\mathcal C}, \int \underline{\mathrm{Coeff}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathcal{B} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}^\times \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \xrightarrow{\text{fixed pts}} \operatorname{Fun}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\int \underline{\mathcal C}, \mathcal{B} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}.
    \]
    Under the first functor, the image of the active arrow $a_{w,c}\colon c \rightarrow w_{\otimes c}$  induces the $W$-arrow $\ell_{w,c}\colon w_* F(c) \rightarrow F{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(w_{\otimes}  c \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}$ under the universal property of cocartesian arrows;
    this arrow is further taken to the fixed points $\ell_{w,c}^W\colon {\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(w_* F(c) \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}^W \rightarrow F(w_\otimes  c)^W$ under the second functor.
    Writing $\widetilde F$ for the Segal object associated with $F$, $\ell_{w,c}^W$ is identified with the cocartesian transport functor of $\mathrm{Un}_{\int \mathcal C}(\widetilde F)$ from the fibre over $c$ along $a_{w,c}$.

    By compositionality of cocartesian lifts, this is moreover restricted from cocartesian transport over $w$ of the composite functor $\int \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \int \underline{\mathcal C} \rightarrow {\operatorname{Span}_{\mathcal{N}}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\left(\mathbb{F}^{\mathcal{T}}_{} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\right)}}$, i.e. the $w$-tensor functor $w_{\otimes}\colon \underline{\mathcal D}^W \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal D}^V$, as desired.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:pullback-partially-lax}
    Fix a cospan of lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed functors $\underline{\mathcal C} \xrightarrow{F} \underline{\mathcal E} \xleftarrow{G} \underline{\mathcal D}$ such that $F$ is an $\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibration.
    This diagram admits a pullback $\mathcal{N}$-normed  $\mathcal{T}$-category $\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{\underline{\mathcal E}} \underline{\mathcal D}$, whose underlying $\mathcal{T}$-category is $U\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{U\underline{\mathcal E}} U\underline{\mathcal D}$;
    moreover, the resulting lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-functor $\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{\underline{\mathcal E}} \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal D}$  is an $\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibration.
    
    Let $(c,d, F(c) \simeq G(d))$ be a $W$-object in $\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{\underline{\mathcal E}} \underline{\mathcal D}$ and $w \colon W \to V$ an $\mathcal{N}$-admissible map. The $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure on $F$ and lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure on $G$ yield an $\underline{\mathcal E}^V$-morphism  
    \[
    F(w_{\otimes }c) \simeq w_{\otimes} F(c) \simeq w_{\otimes} G(d) \to G(w_{\otimes}d).
    \]
    We denote its $F$-cocartesian lift with domain $w_{\otimes}c$ by $f\colon w_{\otimes} c \to \widetilde{w_{\otimes}c}$;
    then $f$ is the lax structure map of  $\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{\underline{\mathcal E}} \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal C}$, and 
     the norm of $(c,d,F(c) \simeq G(d))$ is given by $(\widetilde{w_{\otimes}}c,w_{\otimes}d , F(\widetilde{w_{\otimes}}c)\simeq G(w_{\otimes}d))$.
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Consider the pullback $\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{\underline{\mathcal E}} \underline{\mathcal D}$ in $\mathcal{N}$-operads. 
    Pullback-stability of cocartesian fibrations {\cite[\href{https://kerodon.net/tag/01UF}{Tag 01UF}]{kerodon}} immediately implies that $\underline{\mathcal C} \times_{\underline{\mathcal E}} \underline{\mathcal D} \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal D}$ unstraightens to a cocartesian fibration, so that the pullback is $\mathcal{N}$-normed and the functor an $\mathcal{N}$-normed cocartesian fibration.
    The remaining claims follow straightforwardly by explicitly unwinding {\cite[\href{https://kerodon.net/tag/01UF}{Tag 01UF}]{kerodon}}.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- construction-12: body_md -->

        \underline{\mathcal C} & \longrightarrow \underline{\mathrm{Cat}^{}}^{} \\
        c & \longmapsto \underline{\mathcal D} \times_{\underline{\mathcal C}} {\underline{\mathcal C}}_{/c}
    \end{align*}
    such that, for an $\mathcal{N}$-admissible map $w \colon W \to V$ and a $W$-object $(d,F(d) \to c)$ in the opposite-unstraightening $

As the left arrow is $\mathcal{N}$-normed, we conclude that cocartesian arrows are indeed closed under restriction and norms, as desired.
    The description of the lax $\mathcal{N}$-normed structure follows from combining the descriptions in \Cref{thm:normed-straightening} and \Cref{lem:pullback-partially-lax}.

Given a pair of arrows $A \xrightarrow{m} X \xrightarrow{x} Y$ in $\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{\mathcal{T}}$ such that $x$ is $\mathcal{N}$-admissible, we acquire an essentially unique \textcolor{violet}{distributivity diagram}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:distributivity diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, row sep=tiny, column sep=large]
		\&\& {R} \& {Q} \\
	{\Delta_{m,x} } \& A \\
	\&\& X \& Y
	\arrow["{h}", from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["\epsilon"', from=1-3, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\psi'}"', from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-3, to=3-4]
	\arrow["\psi = x_* m", from=1-4, to=3-4]
	\arrow["\coloneqq"{description}, draw=none, from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["m"', from=2-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["x", from=3-3, to=3-4]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
exhibiting $\psi$ as image of $m$ under the right adjoint of $x^\ast$, i.e. inducing an equivalence
\[
    \mathrm{Map}_{/Y}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\varphi, \psi \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Map}_{/X}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(x^* \varphi, \psi^{\prime} \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)} \xrightarrow{\;\;\; \epsilon^* \;\;\;} \mathrm{Map}_{/X}{\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(x^* \varphi, m \aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)}
\]
for all $\varphi\colon P \rightarrow Y$.
Given $\underline{\mathcal C}$ an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-category, we acquire a commutative diagram
\begin{equation}\label{eq:adjointable}
\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, column sep=tiny]
	\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^Q} \&\&\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{Y}} \\
	{\Psi_{m,x} \coloneqq} \& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{R}} \\
	\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{A}} \&\&\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{X}}
	\arrow["{{\psi^*}}"', from=1-5, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{{h_{\otimes}}}", from=2-2, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{{\epsilon^*}}", from=3-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{{x_{\otimes}}}"', from=3-5, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{{m^*}}", from=3-5, to=3-2]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Given left adjoints $\psi_! \dashv \psi^*$ and $m_! \dashv m^*$, we acquire a Beck-Chevalley transformation
\[
    \beta_{m,x}\colon \psi_!h_{\otimes}\epsilon^* \longrightarrow x_{\otimes} m_!.
\]

<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
Given a map from an orbit $i\colon U \rightarrow Y$ and a diagram $A \xrightarrow{m} X \xrightarrow{x} Y$ with $m$  having fibres in $\mathcal{H}$ and $w$ being $\mathcal{N}$-admissible, we acquire a diagram 
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
	\&\&\& {R_U} \&\& {Q_U} \\
	\& {A_U} \& R \&\& Q \\
	A \&\&\& {X_U} \&\& U \\
	\&\& X \&\& Y
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=3-4]
	\arrow[from=1-4, to=1-6]
	\arrow[from=1-6, to=2-5]
	\arrow["{\psi_U=x_{U *} m_U}", from=1-6, to=3-6]
	\arrow[from=2-2, to=3-1]
	\arrow["{m_U}"'{pos=0.9}, from=2-2, to=3-4]
	\arrow["m"', from=3-1, to=4-3]
	\arrow[from=3-4, to=4-3]
	\arrow["{x_U}"{pos=0.8}, from=3-4, to=3-6]
	\arrow[from=3-6, to=4-5]
	\arrow["x"', from=4-3, to=4-5]
    \arrow[from=2-3, to=2-5, crossing over]
	\arrow["{\psi=x_* m}"{pos=0.2}, from=2-5, to=4-5, crossing over]
    \arrow[from=2-3, to=3-1, crossing over]
	\arrow[from=2-3, to=4-3, crossing over]
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where every square is a pullback diagram and the front and back house-shaped faces are distributivity diagrams;
    so in particular, we acquire a natural transformation $\Delta_{m_U,x_U} \rightarrow \Delta_{m,x}$.
    This yields a natural transformation $\Psi_{m,x} \rightarrow \Psi_{m_U,x_U}$, i.e.
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, row sep=small]
	\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{Q_U}} \&\&\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{U}} \\
	{\underline{\mathcal C}^{Q}} \&\&\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{Y}} \\
	\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{R_U}} \\
	{\underline{\mathcal C}^{R}} \\
	\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{A_U}} \&\&\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{X_U}} \\
	{\underline{\mathcal C}^{A}} \&\&\& {\underline{\mathcal C}^{X}}.
	\arrow[from=1-5, to=1-2, "\psi_U^*"']
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=2-4, to=1-5, "i^*"]
	\arrow[from=3-2, to=1-2, "h_{U,\otimes}"{pos=0.2}]
	\arrow["{{{h_{\otimes}}}}", from=4-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[from=4-1, to=3-2]
	\arrow[from=5-2, to=3-2, "\epsilon_U^*"]
	\arrow[from=5-5, to=1-5, "x_{U,\otimes}"']
	\arrow[from=5-5, to=5-2, "m_U^*"'{pos=0.7}]
	\arrow["{{{\epsilon^*}}}", from=6-1, to=4-1]
	\arrow[from=6-1, to=5-2, "j^*"]
	\arrow[from=6-4, to=5-5]
	\arrow["{{{m^*}}}", from=6-4, to=6-1]
    \arrow["{{{x_{\otimes}}}}"', from=6-4, to=2-4, crossing over]
    \arrow["{{{\psi^*}}}"'{pos=0.3}, from=2-4, to=2-1, crossing over]
\end{tikzcd}
    \]
    We claim that the two Beck-Chevalley conditions are directly related:
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:horrible-BC-diagram}
        \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, row sep=tiny, column sep=small]
	{  i^* \psi_! h_{\otimes} \epsilon^*} \& {i^*\psi_! h_{\otimes} \epsilon^* m^* m_!  } \& { i^*\psi_! \psi^* x_{\otimes} m_!} \& {i^* x_{\otimes} m_!} \\
	{ \psi_{U,!} h_{U,\otimes} \epsilon_U^* j^*} \& {\psi_{U,!} h_{U,\otimes} \epsilon_U^* m_U^* m_{U,!}j^*} \& { \psi_{U,!} \psi_U^* x_{U,\otimes} m_{U,!} j^*} \& {x_{U,\otimes} m_{U,!}j^* }
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\simeq"{marking, allow upside down}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["\simeq"{marking}, draw=none, from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\simeq"{marking, allow upside down}, draw=none, from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-3, to=1-4]
	\arrow["\simeq"{marking, allow upside down}, draw=none, from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\simeq"{marking, allow upside down}, draw=none, from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\simeq"{marking}, draw=none, from=2-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-3, to=2-4]
\end{tikzcd}
    \end{equation}
    Here, the top composite is $i^* \beta_{m,w}$ and the bottom is $\beta_{m_U,w_U} j^*$;
    commutativity follows by commutativity of \eqref{eq:horrible-BC-diagram} together with the fact that $\underline{\mathcal C}$ admits $
   
  \relax  
  \ifmmode
    \expandafter

<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:small-vs-cpct}
    A $\mathcal{T}$-anima is $\kappa$-compact if and only if it is a retract of a $\kappa$-small object;
    if $\kappa$ is uncountable, then this is equivalent to it being $\kappa$-small.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
The first claim is \cite[Prop.~5.3.4.17]{lur09}, and the second follows from the fact that idempotent-splittings are $\aleph_1$-small colimits.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- proposition-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:kappa-restricts}
     If $\kappa$ is a regular cardinal, the following are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}[label={(\alph*)}]
        \item Given a cospan of orbits $U \rightarrow V \leftarrow X$, the pullback $U \times_V X$ is $\kappa$-small.
        \item The inclusions $\mathrm{An}^{V,\mathrm{small}(\kappa)} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{An}^{V}$
        glue together to a $\mathcal{T}$-subcategory.
        \item The inclusions $\mathrm{Cat}^{V,\mathrm{small}(\kappa)} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{V}$ glue together to a $\mathcal{T}$-subcategory.
        \item The subcategory $\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T},\mathrm{small}(\kappa)} \subset \mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}$ is closed under pullbacks.
    \end{enumerate}
    In this case, $\mathrm{An}^{V,\kappa} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{An}^{V}$ and $\mathrm{Cat}^{V,\kappa} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{V}$ form $\mathcal{T}$-subcategories.
<!-- end proposition-23 -->

<!-- proposition-24: body_md -->
\label{prop:kappa-norms}
     If $\kappa$ is a regular cardinal, the following are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}[label={(\alph*)}]
        \item Given a diagram of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} $U \xrightarrow{u} V \xleftarrow{w} W \leftarrow X$, the $U$-anima $u^* w_* X$ is $\kappa$-small.
        \item The inclusions $\mathrm{An}^{V,\mathrm{small}(\kappa)} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{An}^{V}$
        form an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-subcategory.
        \item The inclusions $\mathrm{Cat}^{V,\mathrm{small}(\kappa)} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{V}$ form an $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-subcategory.
    \end{enumerate}
    In this case, $\mathrm{An}^{V,\kappa} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{An}^{V}$ and $\mathrm{Cat}^{V,\kappa} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Cat}^{V}$ form $\mathcal{N}$-normed $\mathcal{T}$-subcategories.
<!-- end proposition-24 -->

<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
Definition 2.2.2.3 in \cite{mwpresentable} obviously implies ours, and ours obviously implies their condition (1).
     In our case, their condition (2) is satisfied for all $\kappa$, since presheaf categories are compactly generated.
     
     Their condition (3) obviously implies $\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}$-normability; compactness is closed under summand inclusion, and applying $W = \varnothing$ shows that $\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}$-normability of $\kappa$-implies that $*$ is $\kappa$-small, so pullback-closure of $\kappa$-smallness implies finite limit closure, completing the identification with Martini-Wolf soundness.
     The identification with the sound doctrine follows by \Cref{lem:small-vs-cpct}.

     Similarly, the comparison with Brink-Lenz follows immediately from the pullback characterisation in \Cref{prop:kappa-restricts}.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- proposition-25: body_md -->
\label{prop:cofinal_embedding}\label{rmk:treg-is-corep}\label{rmk:cofin}
    Let $\upsilon$ be the large regular cardinal of small sets.
    The embedding $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
 \subset  \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ is cofinal and $\upsilon$-small supremum-closed, and each are $\upsilon$-filtered.

    Moreover, if $\mathrm{Sound}_{\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}}$ denotes Martini-Wolf's poset of sound doctrines for the topos $\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}$, then \Cref{cor:everything-is-everything} produces a cofinal full embedding $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
_{\geq \aleph_1} \subset \mathrm{Sound}_{\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}}$.
<!-- end proposition-25 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
First note that $ \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ is $\upsilon$-filtered, since it has small suprema by regularity of $\upsilon$.

    We first prove that there exists an $\mathcal{N}$-normable cardinal.
    Fix a diagram of orbit-finite $\mathcal{T}$-{animæ}{} $U \xrightarrow{u} V \xleftarrow{w} W \xleftarrow{x} X$ with $w$ $\mathcal{N}$-admissible.
    Since the yoneda-image generates $\underline{\mathrm{An}}^{U}$,  $u^* w_* X$ can be expressed as the colimit of a small sequence of small colimit diagrams;
    taking the suprema of the cardinalities of the indexing diagrams yields a cardinality $\overline{\kappa}_{u,v,x}$, and cofinality of regular cardinals in $ \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ allows us to choose regular $\kappa_{u,w,x}$ above it.
    Choosing this uniformly across the small set of triples $(u,v,w)$, we take a supremum
    \[
        \kappa \coloneqq \sup_{u,w,x} \kappa_{u,w,x}.
    \]
    By definition, this is an $\mathcal{N}$-normable regular cardinal, so $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ is indeed nonempty.

    Note that if we have a relation of regular cardinals $\lambda \geq \kappa$ such that $\kappa$ is $\mathcal{N}$-normable, $\lambda$ is  $\mathcal{N}$-normable as well by condition (a) of \Cref{prop:kappa-norms}.
    Now, since $ \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ is well-ordered, $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ has a minimum element $\kappa_{\mathcal{N}}$;
    thus we have
    \[
         \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
 = \mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{reg}}_{\geq \kappa_{\mathcal{N}}} \subset  \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{-norm}}}
.
    \]
    Consequently, cofinality and supremum-closure of $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ are reduced to $\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{reg}}$, where they are well-known.
    $\upsilon$-filteredness of $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
$ then follows from that of $ \ifthenelse{\equal{}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathrm{-norm}}}
$.

    What remains is cofinality of $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
 \subset \mathrm{Sound}_{\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}}$;
    applying cancellation for cofinality {\cite[\href{https://kerodon.net/tag/02N6}{Tag 02N6}]{kerodon}} to the composition $ \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{N}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{N}\mathrm{-norm}}}
 \subset  \ifthenelse{\equal{\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}}{}} 
{\mathrm{Card}}
{\mathrm{Card}^{\mathcal{T}^{\simeq}\mathrm{-norm}}}
 \subset \mathrm{Sound}_{\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}}$ shows that its first inclusion is cofinal, so it suffices to prove this claim when $\mathcal{N} \simeq \mathcal{T}^{\simeq}$.
    Indeed, under the identification with $\mathrm{An}^{\mathcal{T}}$-regularity of \Cref{cor:everything-is-everything}, this is simply \cite[Rmk.~2.2.2.22]{mwpresentable}.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
